messages:
maria: FYI - nightly microbench run (microprobe) shows a regression on H100 for candidate kernel set A. Median 95p latency +12% at seqlen=1024. Uploading profile and perf snippets. https://perf.internal/runs/2421110000
aj: ugh. any immediate signal on KV cache hitrate or batching?
devan: can you paste perf top / flame? even a small hotspot would help isolate kernel vs scheduler
maria: attaching perf snippet: ```
# perf top (sampled)
  32.1%  runtime_kernel_A 
  18.4%  nv_gpu_memcpy_async 
  10.5%  kv_cache_lookup 
   6.2%  batching_scheduler::choose_path
```
ci-bot: nightly-sweep job failed: kbench-candidate-scan exceeded tail-latency threshold on seqlen=1024 for hw=h100 (regress: +12%). See run 2421110000.
aj: nv_gpu_memcpy_async + kv_cache_lookup both up makes me think batching heuristic produced bigger batches or changed prefetch timing -> more NVLink churn
lina: also possible: autotuner picked an ampere-optimized kernel variant that performs worse on long sequences on H100 (different SM scheduling). We saw micro-arch divergence earlier.
devan: quick hypothesis: continuous-batching heuristic is mispredicting sequence-length distribution, pushing some requests to large-batch fastpath which then thrashes KV cache and causes memcpy spikes
maria: ran an isolation job forcing legacy kernel (force-legacy-kernel=true). Command: ```
kbench --kernel=legacy --seq=1024 --iters=600 --hw=h100 --profile=perf.data
```
ops-bot: started job kbench-2421110277-isolate (h100, legacy kernel)
maria: isolation results: forcing legacy kernel drops 95p by 15% vs candidate set A, but avg tokens/sec down ~6% (cost up). KV cache hitrate moves from 0.79 -> 0.91 when using legacy kernel
aj: that nails it to kernel variant interacting badly with kv cache/allocator under long seq lengths
lina: tradeoffs clear: candidate kernel better for short/medium sequences but regresses long tails. Autotuner needs to be seqlen-aware in selection policy rather than global perf numbers
devan: agreed. Proposed fixes: 1) update autotune DB to include per-arch + seqlen buckets (0-128,129-512,513-1024,>1024) 2) add a guard in CI that rejects candidate kernels that degrade 95p on any seqlen bucket by >5% 3) emit seqlen histograms in nightly microbench report for drift detection
aj: also add logging for kv_cache_evictions and per-request memcpy bytes so we can trace thrash correlating with batch path choices
maria: created issue INV-219 for autotune DB + metrics. PR branch: perf/auto-seqlen-weighting
devan: I'll prototype autotune schema update today. Can we re-run full sweep across A100+H100 with new weights before merging?
lina: schedule overnight: we should run both microprobe and a tiny end-to-end workload to capture real kv_cache behavior. Include kv_prefetch toggles (on/off) in runs
aj: command for sweep: ```
./scripts/kbench-sweep --targets=h100,a100 --kernels=candidate_A,legacy --seqs=128,512,1024 --iters=400 --collect=kv_metrics,pprof
```
ops-bot: scheduled job kbench-sweep-2421190000 (target window 02:00-05:00 UTC)
ci-bot: note: adding a seqlen-histogram sanity check to nightly will probably increase CI noise at first until we tune thresholds
maria: fine by me. also FYI KV cache hitrate numbers from failing run: overall hitrate 0.79, eviction_rate ~0.14/request, average prefetch inflight 3.2
aj: please add those numbers to the run metadata so we can query by kernel variant later
maria: done (run metadata updated). Also added a small flame graph and annotated region where nvmemcpy spikes :point_up:
devan: after autotune schema change we should re-run candidate scoring logic: currently score = latency_weight*avg + tail_weight*95p + cost_penalty. Add seqlen-weighted score vector instead of scalar
lina: and add a fallback policy: if worst-case 95p on any seqlen bucket > threshold then prefer conservative kernel for that bucket in routing policy (canary rollout)
maria: filing a follow-up for rollout policy changes — INV-220. I'll re-run the isolation tests tomorrow and paste full perf.data
aj: thanks. can we also add a quick guard in kbench harness to run a small nvlink-stress check to detect memcpy-induced thrash? even 2-3 runs could flag bad combos early
devan: good idea. I'll add a small microprobe that toggles kv_prefetch and measures memcpy bytes per token
maria: nice. thanks team. tagging @aj @devan @lina - will follow up with graphs and PR links in the morning :chart_with_upwards_trend:
